cards.text: This one's a song, baker: a Psalm of Asaph, the man whose name is on it, set to a tune called The Lilies of the Covenant. Don't ask me to hum it, because my mustache starts flapping like it's trying to take off. Asaph opens with “Hear us,” and pictures God leading Joseph like a flock.

cards.question: Asaph pictures God's people as a flock. So what does he call God? O ___ of Israel

cards.text: Asaph calls Him the One who sits enthroned between the cherubim, and asks Him to shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, three of the tribes of Israel. That's not a quiet little prayer from the back of the room, baker; that's a man standing on the counter yelling “OVER HERE!”

cards.question: Asaph has asked the Shepherd of Israel to shine forth. What does he ask God to do with His mighty power?

answers.text: Rally it and come save us
Hold it back a while longer
Turn it on the far mountains

cards.text: Then comes a line Asaph sings more than once, so lean in: “Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us…” Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer, so “shine upon us” hits me RIGHT here.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to restore His people and cause His face to shine upon them. True or false: Asaph asks for this so that they may be saved.

cards.text: Now Asaph calls Him the LORD God of Hosts and asks the question every person staring at an oven timer that WILL NOT MOVE has ever asked: how long?

cards.question: Asaph asks the LORD God of Hosts how long something will go on. What is it?

answers.text: His anger smoldering against their prayers
The famine spreading across the land
The war with the armies of Egypt

cards.question: Asaph describes what life has been like for God's people. What does he say God has given them to eat and drink?

answers.text: Bread of tears and tears to drink
Ashes for bread and bitter water

cards.text: And it's not just trouble at home. Asaph says God makes them contend with their neighbors, like a group chat where every single reply starts a new fight.

cards.question: God makes His people contend with their neighbors, and Asaph says their enemies ___ them

cards.text: And here's that line again, now calling Him the God of Hosts: “Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.”
Now Asaph changes pictures. No more sheep, baker, and I know, I was getting attached too; this time it's a vine God uprooted and moved.

cards.question: Asaph says God uprooted this vine and moved it somewhere new. Where did God pull it up from?
True or false: Asaph says God transplanted the vine into empty land where no nations lived.

cards.text: God clears the ground for it Himself. Baker, I've cleared a LOT of countertops for a batch, but never a whole land.

cards.question: With the ground cleared, Asaph says the vine took ___ and filled the land

cards.text: This vine grows like dough you forgot about overnight. Its shade covers the mountains, and its branches cover the mighty cedars.

cards.question: Asaph's vine keeps on growing. It sends out its branches all the way to the ___

cards.text: Then the song turns. Asaph has a WHY for God, and it's a big one.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says enemies broke down the vine's walls.
With the walls down, everyone passing by picks the vine's fruit. What comes out of the forest to ravage it?

cards.text: But Asaph doesn't stop at why; he turns it into a request and tacks on a “we pray!” When a man says please with an exclamation point, baker, he MEANS it.

cards.question: Asaph begs the God of Hosts to return, to look down from ___ and see, and to attend to the vine

cards.text: Asaph keeps going: “the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.”
Then comes a heavy line about that same vine: “Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.” I think this one hurts to sing.
Then Asaph prays for the son of man God has raised up for Himself. Keep your eye on this line, baker.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to let His hand be upon the son of man. Where does Asaph say this man is?
Asaph asks God to let His hand be upon the man at His right hand. True or false: Asaph says then the people will not turn away from God.
Asaph asks God to revive His people. If He does, what will they do?

cards.text: Asaph ends the song with that line again, and this time he calls on the LORD God of Hosts: “Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.”
